name: dfm_check_envelope
description: DFM check: bounding box of a STEP file against a declared printer build volume. Tessellates the STEP with Gmsh (-2 surface mesh), computes the axis-aligned bounding box from vertex extrema, and reports which axes exceed the declared build volume. Optionally reports mass when density_kg_m3 is supplie

arguments.name: step_path
arguments.desc: Absolute path to the STEP file to analyse.

arguments.name: expected_step_sha256
arguments.desc: Optional SHA-256 expected for the STEP bytes. The tool copies the source into a private snapshot, hashes that copy, and rejects a mismatch.

arguments.name: build_volume_mm
arguments.desc: Declared printer build volume in mm. Explicit — no default.

arguments.name: density_kg_m3
arguments.desc: Material density in kg/m³ (e.g. 2700 for Al 6061, 7850 for steel). Required to compute mass_kg. Omit to skip mass reporting.

arguments.name: mesh_size_mm
arguments.desc: Gmsh surface element size in mm. Coarser is faster for envelope checks (the bounding box is insensitive to tessellation fineness). Pick relative to the smallest feature (e.g. 5 for a 50 mm part).

arguments.name: timeout_ms
arguments.desc: Time limit for the Gmsh subprocess in ms (default 60000).

name: dfm_check_min_thickness
description: DFM check: minimum wall thickness by bidirectional ray casting. Tessellates the STEP with Gmsh (surface STL), then invokes a Python subprocess using Möller-Trumbore ray-triangle intersection in numpy (no trimesh). For each sampled triangle centre, shoots a ray along the inward normal and records the

arguments.name: step_path
arguments.desc: Absolute path to the STEP file.

arguments.name: expected_step_sha256
arguments.desc: Optional SHA-256 expected for the STEP bytes. Mismatch aborts before Gmsh.

arguments.name: min_thickness_mm
arguments.desc: Violation threshold declared by the caller in mm. Only this declared value determines violations — the tool does not apply any process-specific default.

arguments.name: mesh_size_mm
arguments.desc: Gmsh surface element size in mm. Smaller = finer mesh = more accurate but slower. Set to ≤ min_thickness_mm / 2 to reliably detect the thinnest wall.

arguments.name: sample_count
arguments.desc: Number of triangle centres to sample for ray casting (default 500). Higher values improve coverage at the cost of runtime.

arguments.name: cluster_radius_mm
arguments.desc: Spatial radius for merging adjacent violation points into one zone (default: 3× mesh_size_mm).

arguments.name: timeout_ms
arguments.desc: Total time limit in ms covering both Gmsh and Python subprocess (default 120000).

name: dfm_check_overhangs
description: DFM check: surface overhang detection. Tessellates the STEP with Gmsh, then computes the angle between each triangle's outward normal and the declared build_direction. Triangles whose angle from the downward direction (-build_direction) is below max_overhang_deg are violation zones requiring support

arguments.name: step_path
arguments.desc: Absolute path to the STEP file.

arguments.name: expected_step_sha256
arguments.desc: Optional SHA-256 expected for the STEP bytes. Mismatch aborts before Gmsh.

arguments.name: build_direction
arguments.desc: Unit vector of the build direction (printing upward). [0, 0, 1] = +Z upward. Explicit — no default. The downward direction (-build_direction) is used to detect faces that require supports.

arguments.name: max_overhang_deg
arguments.desc: Overhang threshold in degrees from the downward direction. Faces within this angle from downward (-build_direction) are violations. Typical values: 45 (FDM), 30 (SLA/SLS). Explicit — no default.

arguments.name: mesh_size_mm
arguments.desc: Gmsh surface element size in mm. Finer mesh = more accurate overhang area; tighten to 1 mm for small features, use 5–10 mm for large parts.

arguments.name: cluster_radius_mm
arguments.desc: Spatial radius for merging adjacent violation triangles into one zone (default: 3× mesh_size_mm). Larger values produce fewer, coarser zones.

arguments.name: timeout_ms
arguments.desc: Time limit for the Gmsh subprocess in ms (default 60000).
